doc.title: Warren Bernhardt interviewed by Monk Rowe, Bearsville, New York, January 3, 2012

title: Staying open and refusing to be a purist
summary: Classical training kept his ears open; he defends playing with Art Garfunkel and says music is simply good or bad.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well that’s what I was wondering, if starting with classical music somehow opened your ears so that when these other things came along you didn’t shut down to them.

I don’t know. That’s another blessing I guess, how I kept an open mind. Purists never appeal to me. I mean even very great purists. I remember having arguments with Bill about it and him saying, “You should be playing jazz all over the world.” I said, “But I’m playing rock & roll all over, I’m going out with Simon & Garfunkel,” you know, “I’m going to play for six hundred thousand people in Rome.” And he said, “Oh, how can I do that?” I said, “Well you’ve got to stop being a purist is the first thing, and just take what comes along and see if you want to do it.” I studied Tai Chi for quite a few years, there’s a lot of this energy moving around.
Well how did you answer someone if they said well you can never be a real jazz player if you’re going to be associated with Art Garfunkel?

I don’t know, I just played it two weeks ago at the Iridium and I was playing my ass off you know, whatever that’s worth. That’s what my other musicians told me, in the band. I don’t know. One of my first rules, I’ve got very few rules, and one of them was not to be a purist, to be open to other things. Like if music’s good, music’s good. And if music sucks, music sucks. It doesn’t matter if it’s jazz or classical or whatever it is. And I trust, I have faith in my own ear and my heart especially, to learn that difference and only pay attention to the things that are good whenever possible. Once in a while I’d paint myself into a corner and play a McDonald’s hamburger commercial and I said this is not good, but if it’s going to pay a lot of money maybe that’s good.
There was that tuition thing to keep in mind though.
